title: Separate state approximation from a sensing derivative contract
statement: Even exact state agreement at one operating point,and arbitrarily small uniform trace-distance error on a neighborhood,do not certify actual local Fisher information:a smooth prepared family may be constant near t0 while the ideal family has positive information there. For operating-point laws TV(Q,P)<=epsilon and |f|<=L,only |Var_Q(f)-Var_P(f)|<=4L^2 epsilon follows.

requires: Smooth ideal state family and an allowed approximate preparation family
For variance robustness,a bounded common statistic and operating-point TV bound
provides: Smooth plateau/cutoff supplies a positive normalized prepared family with zero derivative at t0
Variance robustness follows from minimizing E(f-c)^2 over c in[-L,L]

For L=O(n) and ideal variance Theta(n^(1+alpha)),epsilon=o(n^(alpha-1)) is sufficient for the worst-case bound4L^2 epsilon to give vanishing relative variance bias;this is not a necessary preparation-accuracy lower bound.
assumptions: A widened variance interval certifies an IDEAL Fisher interval under the ideal theorem;it does not infer the actual derivative
Missing-contract counterexample,not a claim every approximation fails
costs: Acquire derivative/response control,or a finite-displacement decision/risk target at a charged resolution
State fidelity and more repetitions do not supply derivative control
contract.obstruction: No local Fisher lower bound from state closeness alone.
